page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by Alibaba's in-house YiTian710 processor operating at a clock frequency of 2.75 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 64 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present, as the instance features zero GPUs and includes no local NVMe storage, relying on network-attached block volumes over a 10 Gbps baseline network link.

Benchmark results place the ecs.g8y.4xlarge largely within the middle performance tier for general compute tasks, scoring 12841.95 in PassMark CPU tests and 28931.82 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Its memory subsystem demonstrates strong results, registering in the top 25 percent on the PassMark memory evaluation, supported by uncached read throughput of 99.52 GB/sec and write throughput of 47.13 GB/sec. Conversely, the architecture demonstrates weaker relative output in PassMark CPU encryption tests (2628.18) and medium 7B model LLM prompt processing (21.31 tokens/sec), both placing in the bottom quartile of evaluated systems.

The architectural profile provides cost efficiency through dedicated physical ARM cores that eliminate simultaneous multithreading resource contention, delivering predictable execution for containerized microservices, middle-tier enterprise applications, and caching layers like Redis, which reached 26.33 million operations per second. However, workloads requiring intensive cryptographic acceleration, heavy machine learning inference, or high-throughput local scratch storage are constrained by its encryption overhead and lack of local disks. It is best configured for balanced enterprise web serving, compilation, and distributed database services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8y.4xlarge is a general-purpose ARM64 instance powered by a dedicated 16-core Alibaba YiTian710 processor clocked at 2.75 GHz. Configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 64.0 GB of RAM alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes no onboard GPU acceleration and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, it exhibits strong memory subsystem throughput, landing in the top 25 percent of PassMark memory scores, and steady average results in general CPU stress tests and static web throughput. However, encryption benchmarks and medium-scale LLM prompt processing show lower relative performance in the bottom quartile. The ecs.g8y.4xlarge is well suited for balanced enterprise workloads, distributed caching tiers such as Redis, web application hosting, and multi-threaded container deployments that prioritize dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading interference.
